A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CI-CoT/CI-RL study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable matching, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data and PrivacyLens evaluations, model comparisons, reward-weight ablations, and generated examples in Tables 1–4 and appendices A, D, and E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds ConfAIde evaluations in Tables 5–7, plus dataset and output analyses in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The CI-CoT prompt, GRPO training procedure, formatting requirements, and keyword-based rewards remain unchanged. The additional discussion of alternative supervision and customizable policies describes future possibilities, not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds ConfAIde Tiers 1–4, extending evaluation to sensitivity judgments, contextual information-flow judgments, multiparty responses, and meeting summaries. This substantially broadens task coverage beyond the retained synthetic-data and PrivacyLens evaluations, although the addition evaluates only Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical comparator sets, including the DeepSeek distilled models and Claude/Gemini models. ConfAIde extends the existing Qwen2.5-7B baseline-versus-CI-RL comparison. Head-to-head comparisons with AirGapAgent remain proposed future work.

E3.justification: The added ConfAIde evaluation introduces tier-specific protocols: human–model Pearson correlations, string-matched leakage, and meeting-summary leakage/omission measures. Existing data splits, checkpoint selection, training settings, and PrivacyLens judging procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a manual audit of sampled synthetic examples and analyses of output lengths and their association with helpfulness and leakage. Existing reward-weight ablations, LLM/LRM comparisons, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly discloses that repeated experiments were not completed and run-level error bars are unavailable. Appendix F adds output-length dispersion statistics; these describe variation across outputs, not uncertainty in benchmark performance. No increased run count is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain all values, but Tables 5–7 add a substantial body of ConfAIde results. In these new baseline-versus-CI-RL comparisons, Tier 3 leakage is 0.91 versus 0.52 and Tier 4 combined leakage/omission is 0.85 versus 0.45, while omission worsens from 0.10 to 0.15. Appendix F also adds dataset statistics and output-length findings.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, reward definitions in Equations (2)–(3), and existing metric formulas are unchanged. Neither version provides formal theoretical results or proofs; the new ConfAIde measures are empirical evaluation metrics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about CI reasoning, RL training on synthetic data, reduced inappropriate disclosure, preserved utility, and transfer to external benchmarks. ConfAIde supplies additional support without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 adds specific discussion of coarse keyword rewards, evolving norms, user customization, and future integration with privacy gatekeepers. Appendix F interprets weak thinking-length correlations as suggesting potential efficiency benefits. Existing principal interpretations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly documents synthetic-generation temperature 0.7 and dataset/domain/attribute statistics. Checklist item 5 states that code and data were supplied as supplementary material for reviewers; public availability is not established by the PDFs. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, and runtimes are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds five cited works, including TDBench, UTILITY, and work on diffusion/video alignment, and modestly expands Appendix G’s RL discussion. The positioning of CI-RL as complementary to inference-time privacy defenses remains, with additional explanation in Section 7.1.

P1.justification: v2 adds a NeurIPS checklist, acknowledgments, and localized explanatory paragraphs and cross-references. The main narrative, section sequence, terminology, and extensive appendix prompts/examples remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact ConfAIde tables and two dataset-statistics tables. Figure 3 and Tables 1 and 3 move within the document, with accompanying page reflow and minor formatting changes. Existing figures and table designs are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 strengthens validation through another external benchmark and improves transparency about dataset composition, reward limitations, and missing repeated-run uncertainty. The gains are bounded: ConfAIde covers one model, includes an omission tradeoff, and the added audit/correlation analyses lack sample counts or coefficients. These additions modestly improve the paper without substantially resolving its empirical limitations.
